4.

Remove non-return valves

Screw out the non-return valves and remove and discard the O-rings.   
  
Clean the valves and check their functionality with compressed air. Acquire new valves if necessary.

![](manual/58548175-ccef-4d6a-987c-f597b7d4d225/images/jpg/18014402348384395__Web.jpg)

5.

Inspect components

Use a magnifying glass to inspect the plungers, actuator piston sealing ring and cylinder block for wear. Acquire new parts if necessary.  
  
If the sealing ring needs to be replaced, use the sealing ring pushing tool as described.

![](manual/58548175-ccef-4d6a-987c-f597b7d4d225/images/jpg/9007210081869451__Web.jpg)

6.

Place sealing ring on the cone

Slide the cone for the sealing ring onto the actuator piston so that only the lowermost groove is exposed.  
  
Place a new sealing ring on the tapered part of the cone.

![](manual/58548175-ccef-4d6a-987c-f597b7d4d225/images/jpg/19842302987__Web.jpg)

7.

Push down the sealing ring

Slide the pushing tool over the cone thus pushing the sealing ring down into the lowermost groove.  
  
Remove the pushing tool and the cone.

![](manual/58548175-ccef-4d6a-987c-f597b7d4d225/images/jpg/19842305419__Web.jpg)

8.

Compress the sealing ring

Push the compression tool over the actuator piston so that the sealing ring is compressed back to its original form and into the groove.

![](manual/58548175-ccef-4d6a-987c-f597b7d4d225/images/jpg/19842307851__Web.jpg)

9.

Mount the non-return valve

Mount new O-rings on the non-return valves.  
  
Mount the non-return valves in the cylinder block.  
  
 NOTICE There is a non-return valve for each lubrication outlet.  
**Be sure that each non-return valve is tightly screwed into the cylinder block.**

![](manual/58548175-ccef-4d6a-987c-f597b7d4d225/images/jpg/27021601603131019__Web.jpg)

10.

Assemble the cylinder block

query: What precautions should be taken when opening the crankcase or working with flammable materials on an engine?
pos: ﻿ Fire 1. 9836048 2. L9836048 3. Engine data 4. Description 5. D50002-02 6. Fire ### Fire If the crankcase is opened before the engine is cold, welding and the use of naked light will involve the risk of explosions and fire. The same applies to inspection of oil tanks and the space below the cooler. Attention should furthermore be paid to the danger of fire when using paint and solvents with a low flash point. Porous insulating material drenched with oil from leakages is easily inflammable and should be renewed. See also: "Ignition in Crankcase" in section 503/603. 4.

Securing the accumulator tool

Make sure that the pin wrench tool is securely fastened to the engine room deck. This can be done by screwing or welding the flanges of the accumulator tool onto the engine room deck in a convenient place.

![](manual/58548175-ccef-4d6a-987c-f597b7d4d225/images/jpg/9007210570750347__Web.jpg)

5.

Mounting the hook wrench

After the accumulator is securely mounted within the pin wrench, the hook wrench is mounted on the top of the accumulator.   
  
In order to perform this operation, one of the claws has to be removed. The two claws must reach below the ridge on the accumulator.   
  
Once the two claws are in place and the tool is centred, the third claw is to be re-mounted.

![](manual/58548175-ccef-4d6a-987c-f597b7d4d225/images/jpg/9007210570753803__Web.jpg)

6.

Removing the upper part of the accumulator

Insert a piece of pipe in the holes at the end of the wings of the hook wrench to provide leverage.   
  
If the upper piece binds, it can be loosened by tapping (in counter-clockwise direction) a few times with a hammer on the wings of the hook wrench.  
  
Unscrew (in counter-clockwise direction) and remove the upper part of the accumulator.

![](manual/58548175-ccef-4d6a-987c-f597b7d4d225/images/jpg/9007210570756619__Web.jpg)

7.

Dismantling

Remove the defective diaphragm **A**.

![](manual/58548175-ccef-4d6a-987c-f597b7d4d225/images/jpg/18014402356500491__Web.jpg)

8.

Cleaning

Clean both accumulator halves thoroughly, especially the threads, and make sure that the parts are dry afterwards.

Assembly without diaphragm

![](manual/58548175-ccef-4d6a-987c-f597b7d4d225/images/jpg/9007203117452427__Web.jpg)

4.

Check and examine all parts

Clean all the parts of the spindle guide in gas oil and wipe dry with a clean piece of cloth.  
  
Clean all parts again in gas oil or ‘Electrocleaner’ and wipe dry with a clean piece of cloth.  
  
Place all the parts on a clean, soft, lint-free cloth and examine them through an 8–10 times magnification magnifying glass and an inspection lamp.  
  
During the examination, pay special attention to the seating surfaces and sliding surfaces of the parts.

![](manual/58548175-ccef-4d6a-987c-f597b7d4d225/images/jpg/9007203097103371__Web.jpg)

5.

Preparation for polishing

Remove any deposits or very fine scratches by placing the spindle, thrust piece or spindle guide respectively in a lathe, as shown, and polishing with a very fine conventional polishing linen ‘grade 360’.  
  
 NOTICE The sliding surface of the cut-off slide may only be polished very carefully and the sliding surface must not be damaged.  
  
Use also a little oil for the polishing   
  
 NOTICE A coarser polishing linen may NOT be used.  
  
After polishing, clean the parts again and re-check the seat on thrust piece/ spindle, the seat on slide valve/spindle, and the seat on spindle/guide. Use an inspection lamp and an 8–10 times enlargement magnifying glass.  
  
If the seats are not in order, that is, if there are pressing-in marks or similar on the seats, the complete spindle guide must be discarded.

![](manual/58548175-ccef-4d6a-987c-f597b7d4d225/images/jpg/9007203097118987__Web.jpg)

6.

Fuel nozzle cleaning

Clean any carbon deposits from the central bore of the fuel nozzle by means of the special brass brush. Clean the fuel nozzle with gas oil and wipe dry with a clean cloth.

![](manual/58548175-ccef-4d6a-987c-f597b7d4d225/images/jpg/9007203117455243__Web.jpg)

If it is unavoidable, follow the guidelines below: 1. Reduce the amount of fuel in the tank as much as possible before bunkering new fuel. 2. Fuels with similar viscosity, density and pour point often show acceptable compatibility, as they are likely to be of similar fuel type. 3. Check the compatibility of the fuel in the tank and the new fuel: * Use on-board method for indication of compatibility: ASTM D4740 (aka spot-testing or coffee filter testing). * Use lab methods, if the fuels are available. * If the fuels indicate compatibility, mixing may be possible. Note: ASTM D4740 is developed for aromatic fuels containing asphaltenes. Very paraffinic fuels and distillate blends may show false negative results, indicating fuels to be incompatible when they are actually compatible. As the circulating oil cannot by-pass the bottom tank, the whole oil content should partake in the flushing.
